title: How to develop a comprehensive Mangrove Quality Index?
author: Ibrahim, Mohd Yusoff, et al.
materials: formulation of sub-index (MQISi) and Overall MQI; (

steps.title: Acquire and preprocess satellite imagery
steps.instruction: Download the Landsat 8 image for Matang Mangrove Forest Reserve (MMFR) from the USGS website and project it using the Kertau Rectified Skew Orthomorphic (RSO) coordinate system. Record the reserve’s geographic limits: North‑most point 40°56′03.54″ N, 100°28′33.26″ E; South‑most point 40°32′10.81″ N, 100°37′40.54″ E.

steps.title: Classify disturbance levels
steps.instruction: Perform an initial GIS classification of canopy density into four classes (dense, moderately dense, lowly dense, open area). Ground‑truth each class with field observations of logging, recreation, and other activities. Re‑classify the entire MMFR into three disturbance categories: least disturbed, moderately disturbed, and highly disturbed.

steps.title: Define sampling transects
steps.instruction: Within each of the four management zones (Kuala Sepetang North, Kuala Sepetang South, Kuala Trong, Sungai Kerang) select four sites representing the three disturbance levels. At each site lay a 100 m transect from the riverbank inland and mark sampling plots every 20 m (i.e., at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 m).

steps.title: Collect field measurements
steps.instruction: At every plot record the following:

substeps.instruction: Measure tree height (m), basal area (m²/ha), tree volume (m³/ha), and aboveground biomass (tonne/ha). Count crab abundance in the soil.
Take a soil sample for laboratory analysis of nitrogen (N), carbon (C), sulphur (S), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), magnesium (Mg), calcium (Ca) (all μg g⁻¹) and soil pH.

Collect a water sample at upstream, middle‑stream, and downstream points for electrical conductivity (µS cm⁻¹), dissolved oxygen (DO, mg L⁻¹), pH, turbidity (NTU), total dissolved solids (mg L⁻¹), temperature (°C), and total suspended solids (mg L⁻¹).

Perform monthly plankton sampling at designated stations; preserve samples for laboratory identification and enumeration of phytoplankton, diatoms, dinoflagellates, copepods, and jellyfish (species count and cells ml⁻¹).

Interview 300 local fishermen in December 2015 at several jetties to record fish landing (kg day⁻¹), time spent fishing (hours), fishing effort (days week⁻¹), monthly income (USD person⁻¹), age (years), and education level (years).

steps.title: Analyze laboratory samples
steps.instruction: Use standard methods to determine for each soil sample: N, C, S, P, K, Mg, Ca concentrations (μg g⁻¹) and pH. For each water sample determine EC (µS cm⁻¹), DO (mg L⁻¹), pH, turbidity (NTU), TDS (mg L⁻¹), temperature (°C), TSS (mg L⁻¹), chemical oxygen demand (COD, mg L⁻¹), biochemical oxygen demand (BOD, mg L⁻¹), salinity (%), ammonia (NH₃, mg L⁻¹), phosphate (PO₄, mg L⁻¹), nitrate (NO₃, mg L⁻¹), and fecal coliform (mg L⁻¹). Process plankton samples to obtain species composition and cell counts per ml.

steps.title: Perform PCA on each category
steps.instruction: For each of the five socio‑ecological categories run a principal component analysis (no rotation, based on the correlation matrix) on the relevant variables:

substeps.instruction: Biotic integrity: tree height, basal area, tree volume, aboveground biomass, crab abundance – select aboveground biomass and crab abundance (91 % cumulative variation).
Soil index: N, C, S, P, K, Mg, Ca, pH – select soil nitrogen and soil carbon (≈79 % variation).

Marine‑mangrove: phytoplankton species & abundance, diatom species & abundance, dinoflagellate species & abundance, copepod species & abundance, jellyfish species & abundance – select number of phytoplankton species and number of diatom species.
Hydrology: EC, DO, pH, turbidity, TDS, temperature, TSS – select turbidity and dissolved oxygen.
Socio‑economic: fish landing, time spent, fishing effort, income, age, education – select time spent and education level.

steps.title: Calculate sub‑index weights
steps.instruction: For each selected metric within a category:

substeps.instruction: Determine the proportion of variance explained (pᵢ) for its principal component.
Multiply pᵢ by the component score (Sᵢ) to obtain pSᵢ.
Sum all pSᵢ values to get w_T = Σ pSᵢ.
Compute the weight wᵢ = pSᵢ / w_T.
Calculate the mean (x̄) and standard deviation (s) of the raw measurements for the metric.
Standardize each observation: zᵢ = (xᵢⱼ – x̄ᵢ) / sᵢ.
Multiply the weight by the standardized value and by 2 (because two metrics are used): 2 wᵢ zᵢ.
Sum the products for the two metrics to obtain the category sub‑index: MQISᵢ = Σ 2 wᵢ zᵢ.

steps.title: Derive overall MQI
steps.instruction: Repeat the weighting and standardization steps for all five categories (biotic integrity, soil, marine‑mangrove, hydrology, socio‑economic). Sum the five category scores:

substeps.instruction: Overall MQI = Σ_{i=1}^{5} MQISᵢ.
Classify the overall score: 1 (worst) if ≤1.5, 2 (bad) if >1.5‑2.5, 3 (moderate) if >2.5‑3.5, 4 (good) if >3.5‑4.5, 5 (excellent) if >4.5.

steps.title: Summarize MQI by disturbance level
steps.instruction: Create a table (as in Table 2) showing for each disturbance level (least, moderately, most) the environment component (MQIₑ) and socio‑economic component (MQIₛₑ). Include the variable scores, e.g., Above Ground Biomass 4 (21.47; 39.00) for least disturbed, Crab Abundance 3 (32.00; 70.00) for moderate, etc., and the final overall MQI values (e.g., 5 42 a random value for: (Variable 1; Variable 2)).

steps.title: Validate MQI with NDVI
steps.instruction: Generate a Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) map from a recent SPOT image (1.5 m resolution) using ERDAS 2014. Extract NDVI values for each sampled site and compare with MQI rankings:

substeps.instruction: Disturbance rank 2: NDVI –0.916 to 0.315.
Disturbance rank 4: NDVI –0.732 to 0.638.
Disturbance rank 5: NDVI –0.689 to 0.652.
Interpret NDVI near 1 as dense vegetation (supports higher MQI) and near –1 as sparse vegetation (supports lower MQI). Confirm that NDVI trends agree with the computed MQI values.
